questions.stem: Find the area of a sector with radius 5 cm and central angle 60°.
questions.solution: The area of a sector is given by (central angle in radians / 2π) × πr². First, convert the central angle to radians: 60° = π/3 radians. Then calculate the area: (π/3 / 2π) × π(5 cm)² = (1/6) × 25π cm² = 1.25π cm².
questions.explanation: The formula for sector area is used correctly, and the conversion from degrees to radians is done accurately.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be forgetting to convert the central angle to radians before plugging it into the formula.

questions.stem: What is the area of a sector with radius 7 cm and central angle 120°?
questions.solution: The area of a sector is given by (central angle in radians / 2π) × πr². First, convert the central angle to radians: 120° = 2π/3 radians. Then calculate the area: (2π/3 / 2π) × π(7 cm)² = (1/3) × 49π cm² = 49π/3 cm² ≈ 21π cm².
questions.explanation: The formula for sector area is applied correctly, and the conversion from degrees to radians is done accurately.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be using the wrong central angle value in the calculation.

questions.stem: Find the area of a sector with radius 9 cm and central angle π/4 radians.
questions.solution: The area of a sector is given by (central angle / 2π) × πr². In this case, the central angle is already in radians. Calculate the area: (π/4 / 2π) × π(9 cm)² = (1/8) × 81π cm² = 81π/8 cm² ≈ 1.5π cm².
questions.explanation: The formula for sector area is used correctly without any conversion, as the central angle is already in radians.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be multiplying by π twice instead of dividing by 2π.

questions.stem: Find the area of a sector with radius 18 cm and central angle 2π radians.
questions.solution: The area of a sector with a central angle of 2π radians is the entire circle, so the area is πr². Calculate the area: π(18 cm)² = 324π cm².
questions.explanation: The formula for sector area is applied correctly, recognizing that a full revolution corresponds to the entire circle.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be thinking that the area of the sector would be less than the area of the whole circle.
